dedupe_keys.name: pypsa python for power system analysis

description: PyPSA is an open-source Python framework for optimising and simulating power and multi-carrier energy systems. It implements economic dispatch with unit commitment, linear optimal power flow in meshed AC-DC networks with optional loss approximations, security-constrained optimal power flow under N-1 line outages, single and multi-period capacity expansion planning, two-stage stochastic optimisation, modelling to generate alternatives, sector coupling (heat, hydrogen, electric vehicles, synthetic fuels) and full non-linear Newton-Raphson power flow. Maintenance is led by the Department of Digital Transformation in Energy Systems at the Technical University of Berlin with funding from the German Research Foundation; earlier versions were developed at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology and FIAS. The framework is generic and location independent: users supply network components and time series for any country or region, from a district to a continent, at any temporal resolution. It is distributed as a package on PyPI (version 1.3.0, August 2026, Python 3.11 or newer) and conda-forge, with source code on GitHub and documentation at docs.pypsa.org, under the MIT licence and free of charge. Caveats: its documented features are steady-state power flow and optimisation, with no dynamic stability or transient simulation listed, and optimisation runs need a solver (HiGHS is installed by default; GLPK, CBC or commercial solvers such as Gurobi can be used). Simulation uses are capacity planning, optimisation, network flow and resilience studies of transmission and distribution grids. Related records: it underlies model-pypsa-eur and complements model-pandapower, which can exchange networks with it.
